sessions.title: Contemporary for Over 60s

sessions.title: Line Dancing Beginners
sessions.details: Hold ‘em like they do in Texas with our new line dance class. Learn a range of short, up tempo line dance routines to a range of music including Country & Western classics from the likes of Dolly Parton and Shania Twain, to current TikTok trends like Boots on the Ground and House of Bamboo. Heel tapping, thigh slapping and suitable for all experience and fitness levels, this class is all the Thursday evening fun you need to get ready for the weekend. Wear whatever is comfortable but to save our lovely dance floors, please wear jazz shoes or light soled trainers and leave your cowboy boots at the door. sure you have removed jewellery before class, and long hair is tied back. Suitable if: you are 18+ and comfortable with the basics of Ballet and want to progress your technique with new challenges and combinations. We'd recommend around one year of ballet experience for this class. Building Information Classes take place at Rambert, 99 Upper Ground SE1 9PP. We have a fully accessible building, including accessible toilets and showers. There is on-street parking for Blue Badge holders with step-free access to the building, and lifts to all levels. Changing facilities are available on the first floor. A water fountain is available on the second floor- please bring your own reuse-able bottle for this. You can wear whatever your are comfortable moving in, and you’re welcome to wear dance shoes if you have them (although no dark/black soles) or bare-feet. sessions.title: ProDance Class with Ozzy & Tiegan
sessions.details: Sweat, Strength and Totality - the journey of class. Through diving into sensation and groove, we will explore story telling as we find humour, character and individuality through improvisational research. Class with explore a range of textures and images as we move through guided improvisation, engaging the core challenging the body. Through crossings and set phrases we will explore the totality of movement, from the smallest gesture to the largest groove, as we move through character and humour driven phrases. This is a space for fun and accessible play, to research and laugh together.

sessions.title: HANDSTAND LAB
sessions.details: Inversions are a fun and challenging way of building strength and challenging the mind. If you are starting your handstand journey but are struggling to kick up and catch the balance or are married to the wall, these are perfect classes for you. We will learn some wrist, shoulder and body tension conditioning drills and unpick how we kick up to a handstand. We will touch on how to safely fall out of a handstand and discuss how important tackling fear is. We will work in partners and small groups to support each other.

sessions.title: Saturday CI Workshop: Performing Oneself
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • This workshop is about being an audience and having an audience. Showing up and witnessing. Seeing and being seen, being yourself and being in a group. The focus will not be on looking good but rather on the way in which being seen supports us in seeing ourselves. We will frame witnessing each other dance as an expanded way of connecting. We will investigate relating to multiple partners at the same time and getting in and out of contact with a partner while maintaining the integrity of our own dance. We will move on to ensemble scores for improvising together. We will look at turning our own desires into action and how these individual expressions of creativity can coexist in a shared space with others. Issues or blocks related to fear, failure, taking space and confusion will be welcomed and fuel the training of our agency and awareness. As always with my workshops, you can choose your own level of challenge. Technical study will evolve into free Contact Dancing, where we can explore and integrate new learnings into improvisation. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-sn3d0-20260516143000

sessions.details: Room 154, Richard Hoggart Building, Goldsmiths, Lewisham Way, London, SE14 6NW • A two hour Contact Improvisation class starting at 13:00 class followed by a jam at 15:00 finishing at 18:00. These Small Things This class explores some of the small moves that can form the fabric of a contact dance: scoops, tilts and see-saws that allow a tiny moment of uplift or sweep us gently off our feet. Starting with a solo warm-up of movement patterns and structured improvisations, we will move to partner tasks which encourage exploration and problem-solving. As we dance together these small exchanges can develop into bigger moves…or perhaps instead foster an appreciation of the ‘unspectacular’. Jo Dyer is a dancer and teacher, who has trained predominantly in release-based contemporary dance and improvisation. She has practised contact improvisation for many years and trained at Nancy Stark Smith’s January workshop in 2006. Her choreographic work includes A Tin Drum (Impulstanz Salzburg), Viva la Vida (Linbury Theatre) and Threefold (finalist at masdanza). Jo recently completed a MA in Creative Practice at TrinityLaban, with a Leverhulme Trust Dance Scholarship, where her final project investigated using contact improvisation to make politically engaged performance. CLASS DESCRIPTION: Do you want to limit your injury risk, while also building strength to become a better dancer? This fitness class will help you substantially improve your posture and correct any issues relating to your body alignment. It is very easy to create bad habits in ballet, so changing these habits often requires retraining muscle memory. Christina's Posture Power with PBT elements class will not only help you build up more strength and flexibility, but will also help you train the muscle memory required for automatically performing movements the right way. This class will be accompanied by music. With her experience as a coach, ballet teacher and approved PBT instructor, Christina has put together a class that will help you limit your injury risk and become a stronger and better dancer. It is also a perfect preparation for her 11:30 Int/Adv ballet class which takes place right after her Posture Power with PBT elements class. Progressing Ballet Technique (PBT) is an innovative programme which was developed by Marie Walton- Mahon in order to help dancers and students improve their technique. CLASS DESCRIPTION This class will follow the traditional structure of the codified technique, sequencing through a set series of seated floor exercises, standing exercises and across-the-floor sequences. The Graham Technique is an immensely valuable technique to layer on top of any dance training as it emphasises the importance of the usage of the back, as well as accessing the deep core abdominal muscles.Fundamental principles in Graham Technique are the contraction and release, opposition, shift of weight and spirals. Graham dancers believe that it is important that we not simply see ourselves as objects in space when dancing, but that we expand their body, energy and focus so they are amplified enough to fill that space. The class will serve to free up the back, open up the hips and the body. On top, form the dancer to find dynamics, intricacy and articulation of the spine. Minimum age: 16

It is built to feel accessible from the start, with a structure that helps you settle in quickly and build confidence as you go. One of the reasons this class works so well for beginners is that choreography begins early in the session, including from the warm-up. That means you are not left watching for too long or overthinking what to do. Instead, you are gently supported into copying, moving and feeling comfortable in the room right away. The class supports confidence, coordination, enjoyment and expression all at once. It is suitable for most fitness levels, and it is designed to help people who may not yet feel like dancers begin to trust their bodies, their memory and their ability to learn. If you have never danced before, you can expect clear guidance, repetition, encouragement and a friendly pace. You do not need to arrive knowing the steps, knowing the counts or knowing what kind of dancer you are. You simply need to come willing to try. Who it’s for Complete beginners. People returning to dance after a break. Adults looking for a welcoming, low-pressure space to move. Anyone who wants to build confidence alongside coordination and expression. What to expect You will be guided through a short introduction, accessible warm-up, simple choreography and movement that is designed to help you learn by doing. It is not yoga. Instead, it is a guided group fitness session built to improve flexibility, mobility and range of motion through focused, full-body stretching techniques. The class combines static stretching, dynamic movement and PNF-style contract-relax work, making it both restorative and functional. It is designed for people who want to carve out time to stretch properly, without rushing and without needing to fit it into a bigger dance or fitness class. The women-only environment adds an extra layer of comfort and relatability, making it easier to switch off, settle in and focus on your own body. By the end of the session, you should feel physically lighter, taller, more open and less stiff, with a calmer mind and a stronger sense of connection to your body. Because stretching time is often overlooked in busy schedules, this class creates a rare space where you can slow down, move with care, and leave feeling both released and re-energised. Who it’s for Women who want a calm, private, and comfortable space to stretch. Women who want to improve flexibility, mobility and range of motion. Women who prefer a guided stretch session rather than yoga. Women who want time to release tension and reset. sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. Suitable for most levels, this class is a beautiful way to care for your body, move more freely, and give yourself the reset you didn’t know you needed.

sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-sis0w-20260518183000

sessions.title: Monday Contact Improv Jam + modular music with Rocio Ayllón and Sami Sabik
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 5SQ • Please note they won't be an intro circle anymore. First timers can arrive a bit earlier for any questions and info around consent or about the jam. I also advise newcomers to familiarise themselves with the guidelines. Jam The emphasis of the jam is to explore movement while being in physical contact with other movers. Participants are encouraged to experience it as an embodied research and a practice where everyone can bring their own research, interest and physicality into the space. Jamming is the best way to try out, take risks, learn from each other, observe, connect, be surprised, practice setting boundaries, dance and play with people we may not know or expect to dance with. Participants are asked to take responsibility for themselves. Levels and abilities: The space welcomes professional dancers, amateurs, seasoned contact improvisers and beginners, people from all backgrounds and abilities. It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. Event page: https://millco.co.uk/events/contact-improvisation-jam/ https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-s65v7-20260518183000

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1 (Course of 5 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-sis0w-20260518183000

sessions.title: ProDance Class with Orla Hardie
sessions.details: Orla’s teaching practice is an exploration of the imagination, using texture and self-caricature as pathways to connect to movement. Supported by an array of music genres and guided improvisation, we will move through a range of dynamics from gooey totality to squeaky articulation. Moving through set material, we’ll dissolve in and out of the floor, getting down, sweaty, and fully immersed. Together we create a space where we can dive into the mind, liberate the body, and play.

sessions.title: ROCKET
sessions.details: Rocket is deeply rooted in Ashtanga. It is a series of standing, balancing and inverted postures all linked by vinyasas (movement flows), incorporating basic poses with challenging arm balances, inversions and back bends Inversions are lot of fun, but they also prove to be some of the most challenging postures. Some of the upside down postures are designed to energise us, others are designed to calm us down. No matter if you are a newbie or an old hat to inversions this class will be fun, will get you sweating and see the world from another perspective -upside down.

sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • A Calling Home – The Body as Home is a Somatic Activated Healing™ (SAH Method) practice, a trauma-informed, body-based approach that blends: somatic movement breath work mantra and meditation music and free, intuitive movement.Rather than intellectualizing or talking about emotions, this practice invites the body to lead, allowing sensations and stored emotions to be expressed and gently released through movement. We work from a bottom-up approach, using the body and felt sensations as the entry point, rather than analyzing thoughts or revisiting specific traumatic memories. As a certified SAH Method™ teacher, I guide participants to “drop the story and be with the feeling,” creating a safe space for emotions to move without re-engaging with the narratives around them. Participants can expect a guided, supportive experience that helps to: ground and regulate the nervous system reconnect with physical sensations gently release what has been held in the body cultivate moments of safety, steadiness, and embodied presence There is no choreography, no performance, and no “right way” to move. This session is an invitation to move, shake, soften, and play, to let energy flow more freely through the body, release what feels stuck, and reconnect with joy, aliveness, and a sense of home within.Still wondering what to expect? sessions.title: Mixed All Levels Class
sessions.details: Laban Building • Creekside, London, SE8 3DZ, UK, London • This mixed all-levels class is designed to bring together people with different dance backgrounds in one shared space. The class is less technical and places more emphasis on feeling expressive, present and connected in the room. The balance here is roughly 70% expression and 30% technique. That means there is still structure, clarity and growth, but there is also plenty of room for alternative movement and individual interpretation. The session is adaptable, so beginners and more experienced dancers can both engage meaningfully without the class feeling too difficult or too simple. This class is especially valuable for the sense of community it creates. You are not being measured only by ability level; instead, you are welcomed into a space where different types of movers can push, motivate and inspire one another. If you are unsure whether this class is for you, it is usually best to start with a beginner class and then speak to a member of the 1Syllable team, or email us, so we can help guide you to the right level. Who it’s for Adults of different dance backgrounds who want a shared class experience. People who want expression, creativity and community alongside movement. Beginners who are ready for more space and variety. More experienced dancers who want a class that feels open, adaptable and motivating. What to expect You will move through a short introduction, warm-up, guided movement and choreography that can be adapted to different experience levels. The class prioritises expression and community while still offering enough structure to help you grow. Every ticket includes a goody bag and professional filming is available for anyone who would like. Outcome You leave feeling challenged, supported, creatively open and part of a community that values expression as much as ability. Practical note Please arrive 10–15 minutes early so you can settle in and get familiar with the space before class begins. If you are pregnant, postnatal or managing an injury, please let the team know in advance so adjustments can be made. What to Wear Anything you feel comfortable in and able to stretch freely. This class is 18+ only. By purchasing a ticket, you agree to these terms and conditions.

CLASS DESCRIPTION: Do you want to limit your injury risk, while also building strength to become a better dancer? This fitness class will help you substantially improve your posture and correct any issues relating to your body alignment. It is very easy to create bad habits in ballet, so changing these habits often requires retraining muscle memory. Christina's Posture Power with PBT elements class will not only help you build up more strength and flexibility, but will also help you train the muscle memory required for automatically performing movements the right way. This class will be accompanied by music. With her experience as a coach, ballet teacher and approved PBT instructor, Christina has put together a class that will help you limit your injury risk and become a stronger and better dancer. Posture Power with PBT elements is a general level class and therefore suitable for those, who either wish to improve their ballet technique or simply improve their fitness level. It is also a perfect preparation for her 11:30 Int/Adv ballet class which takes place right after her Posture Power with PBT elements class. Progressing Ballet Technique (PBT) is an innovative programme which was developed by Marie Walton- Mahon in order to help dancers and students improve their technique. The programme includes carefully designed exercises focusing on training muscle memory and improving core strength, weight placement and alignment of the body. Minimum age: 14

The Graham Technique is an immensely valuable technique to layer on top of any dance training as it emphasises the importance of the usage of the back, as well as accessing the deep core abdominal muscles.Fundamental principles in Graham Technique are the contraction and release, opposition, shift of weight and spirals. Graham dancers believe that it is important that we not simply see ourselves as objects in space when dancing, but that we expand their body, energy and focus so they are amplified enough to fill that space. The class will serve to free up the back, open up the hips and the body. On top, form the dancer to find dynamics, intricacy and articulation of the spine. Minimum age: 16

sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. Suitable for most levels, this class is a beautiful way to care for your body, move more freely, and give yourself the reset you didn’t know you needed.

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1 (Course of 5 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-srouz-20260525183000

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1 (Course of 5 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-srouz-20260525183000

sessions.title: ROCKET
sessions.details: Rocket is deeply rooted in Ashtanga. It is a series of standing, balancing and inverted postures all linked by vinyasas (movement flows), incorporating basic poses with challenging arm balances, inversions and back bends Inversions are lot of fun, but they also prove to be some of the most challenging postures. Some of the upside down postures are designed to energise us, others are designed to calm us down. No matter if you are a newbie or an old hat to inversions this class will be fun, will get you sweating and see the world from another perspective -upside down.

sessions.title: Rueda Libre Wednesday + Libre Class • Timba con Afro with Osbanis + Anneta •
sessions.details: Coal Drops Yard, Coal Drops Yard, King's Cross, London, N1C 4DQ, United Kingdom • Join Us for an Unforgettable Outdoor Cuban Salsa Event! Get ready to dance, learn, meet amazing people, and embrace the joy of salsa dancing! Our outdoor salsa event is the perfect place to spice up your evening, whether you’re a seasoned pro or have never danced a step in your life. Here’s what to expect: Cuban Salsa and Rueda Classes: We’re offering classes for all levels, from absolute beginners to advanced dancers. No partner? No problem! Everyone is welcome to join in the fun. Visit https://ruedalibre.co.uk/classes/ to find out which class level suits you best. Class Time: Classes kick off at 7:00 PM, but make sure to arrive by 6:45 PM to show your QR code and collect your wristband. This ensures you’re ready and wont miss the beginning of the class. Free Outdoor Social Dancing: After the class, the night doesn’t end! Stick around for some free outdoor social dancing. Practice your moves, connect with the community, and just let loose. The vibe is 10/10 so enjoy it. Affordable Pricing: Classes start at just £9 (excluding fees), and you’ll have the chance to practice what you’ve learned during the session. The most budget-friendly way to pay is via our QR code in person, no fees to worry about. Prefer other options? We also accept cash, contactless payments, and online payments for your convenience. sessions.title: FLEXIBILITY/BACKBENDS

It’s really about learning how to align your joints effectively while lengthening your muscles over time. In fact, when working on deeper ‘backbends’, most of the focus will be on the anterior line. It should be called the heart-opening class because that’s what it does, in every sense of the word. ****GET the 4x CLASS PACK for £50

sessions.details: In this class, James guides participants through improvisation practices that encourage honesty, curiosity, and personal expression through movement. Together, we will explore how to connect more deeply with ourselves, our bodies, and each other in a supportive and open environment. sessions.title: 'ReSourcing your CI Practice: what moves you?' Workshop with Colleen Bartley
sessions.details: Room 154, Richard Hoggart Building, Goldsmiths, Lewisham Way, London, SE14 6NW • ReSourcing your CI Practice: what moves you? Working with foundational principles of CI this workshop explores Contact Improvisation as research into deep listening, tuning the senses and attention, emergent composition and self awareness. Over the course of the day we will explore quiet perceptual practices and more dynamic dancing, creating space for reflection, experimentation and embodied decision-making. Through touch, movement and attention, we will investigate how dances arise from changing relationships — between bodies, gravity, sensation, imagination and space. We'll explore how life moves through evolutionary patterns and work with materials from Nancy Stark Smith, Steve Paxton, Nita Little and other founders of CI with influences from Lisa Nelson, and Caryn McHose. The day will include solo, duet and group practices, scores, improvisational structures and time for reflection. We will explore responsiveness, composition in the moment, and ways of expanding perception through movement. We welcome curiosity, experimentation and different physical experiences. The class aims to cultivate an inclusive environment for curiosity, exploration, embodied research, critical reflection, dialogue and dancing together. Sources/Influences: Tuning Scores, Experiential Anatomy, The Underscore, Instant Composition, Neurological diversity, post-modern dance, Evolutionary Biology, BMC, Somatic Education, Relational Intelligence, Embryology, Functional Movement Colleen Bartley has a Dance and Education degree from Swarthmore College and a diploma in Community Dance from Laban with years of experience with Somatic Education. She co-organised London Contact Improvisation and was a co-editor at Contact Quarterly. She has worked directly with most of the founders of Contact Improvisation and been influenced by teachers of contemporary and post-modern dance, experiential anatomy with Gary Carter and Caryn McHose, Authentic Movement with Susan Schell, Improvisation & Composition (Tuning Scores with Lisa Nelson, The Underscore with Nancy Stark Smith, Ensemble Thinking with Nina Martin, Relational Intelligence with Nita Little) and is very active in dancing, organizing, writing about and documenting dance. Colleen has an invisible disability which informs her practice as a teacher and an artist. She believes that its everyone’s birthright to move, that people are inherently creative, movement is our first language, and sees dance as a way to empower people, to effect social change and to build community. sessions.title: PARTNERING WORKSHOP
sessions.details: This contemporary partnering workshop explores trust, communication, and physical connection through movement. Beginning with a guided warm-up focused on mobility, strength, and stability, participants will prepare their bodies with floorwork, weight transfer, spinal articulation, and gentle inversions. We then move into partner-based exercises that build trust and awareness through weight-sharing and safe, supportive grips. As confidence develops, participants will explore the mechanics of lifting and being lifted, breaking down technique to ensure accessibility, safety, and clarity for all bodies. The session culminates in learning a collaborative movement phrase, integrating the skills developed throughout the workshop while encouraging communication and adaptability between partners. This class creates a supportive environment where participants can expand their movement vocabulary, deepen connection, and discover new possibilities within partnering work.

This fitness class will help you substantially improve your posture and correct any issues relating to your body alignment. CLASS DESCRIPTION This class will follow the traditional structure of the codified technique, sequencing through a set series of seated floor exercises, standing exercises and across-the-floor sequences. The Graham Technique is an immensely valuable technique to layer on top of any dance training as it emphasises the importance of the usage of the back, as well as accessing the deep core abdominal muscles.Fundamental principles in Graham Technique are the contraction and release, opposition, shift of weight and spirals. Graham dancers believe that it is important that we not simply see ourselves as objects in space when dancing, but that we expand their body, energy and focus so they are amplified enough to fill that space. The class will serve to free up the back, open up the hips and the body. On top, form the dancer to find dynamics, intricacy and articulation of the spine. Minimum age: 16

sessions.details: Laban Building • Creekside, London, SE8 3DZ, UK, London • This women-only beginner class is built around movement, rather than by a heavy beat or familiar lyrical structure. Instead of music, the class uses vocals and/or nasheeds, offering a different kind of soundscape for movement that feels stripped back, open and deeply personal. The class is ideal for women who want to step away from secular music or music altogether, and for those who are looking for a space that feels culturally sensitive, private and genuinely welcoming. It is also a beautiful option for women who want to experience dance in a different way, where the body, mind and breath have more space to lead. Movement in this class can feel soft, expressive, grounding, or whatever it needs to be for you. Because there is less sound to lean on, the class creates an eye-opening experience: you are invited to trust your own instincts, your own rhythm and your own interpretation. That can feel honest, freeing and surprisingly liberating. The atmosphere values community, uplift and comfort, so you can come solo or with a friend and feel held in the room. Who it’s for Women looking for a safe, private and culturally sensitive space to dance for the first time or return to movement after a break. Those who value community as much as the dance itself, whether they come solo or with a friend. Women who prefer to move without secular music or without music altogether. Women who want a different sound and a different relationship to movement. What to expect You will begin with a short introduction before moving into a beginner-friendly session that includes guided movement, simple choreography and space for self-expression. The class is designed to help you feel comfortable, supported and free to move at your own pace. Outcome You leave feeling grounded, liberated and more connected to your own movement, with a stronger sense of confidence and self-expression. Practical note Please arrive 10–15 minutes early so you can settle in and get familiar with the space before class begins. Suitable for most fitness levels. If you are pregnant, postnatal or managing an injury, please let the team know in advance so adjustments can be made. What to Wear Anything you feel comfortable in and able to move freely. This class is 18+ only. By purchasing a ticket, you agree to these terms and conditions.

sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1+2 (Course of 11 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 (Beginners 1) And Mondays 01/06, 08/06, 15/06, 22/06, 29/06 and 06/07 (Beginners 2) from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. Beginners 1: The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. Beginners 2: It will build on what we started in Beginners 1, deepening your understanding of the basics and developing more vocabulary for giving and receiving weight, moving in close connection with the floor, rolling and falling. We will work on expanding confidence in: Expressing what you want and do not want in your partner dances Creativity and playfulness Starting and finishing dances Deep physical listening Dancing in trios Lifting and being lifted Jamming skills I will be working with new material, so it will be a way of revisiting the fundamentals while learning new pathways. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-smfda-20260601183000

sessions.title: Monday Contact Improv: Class + Jam
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 5SQ • Doors open at 6.20pm Please note they won't be an intro circle anymore. First timers can arrive a bit earlier for any questions and info around consent or about the jam. I also advise newcomers to familiarise themselves with the guidelines. This week we have a class taught by Marie, an experienced CI practitioner (22 years), professional dancer and choreographer. Theme and Content The theme of the class will be posted closer to the time in the CI Monday Jam WhatsApp group. You can join in following this link: https://chat.whatsapp.com/Iivbz8LzDvK5lGkiitQgcH (please note I will ask you a few question about yourself before I allow you into the chat, when you join please introduce yourself so we know who's in the chat) These Contact Improvisation classes give participants tools to be in touch and communicate through touch, and feel more confident joining a jam. There are open levels and benefit beginners, improvers and experienced practitioners. There is a mix of somatic guided exploration to be embodied, usually in solo, some mindful and focused explorations with one or several partners, and some more technical tools or short patterns. This will be followed by a 45min-1h jam Jam The emphasis of the jam is to explore movement while being in physical contact with other movers. Participants are encouraged to experience it as an embodied research and a practice where everyone can bring their own research, interest and physicality into the space. Jamming is the best way to try out, take risks, learn from each other, observe, connect, be surprised, practice setting boundaries, dance and play with people we may not know or expect to dance with. Participants are asked to take responsibility for themselves. Levels and abilities: The space welcomes professional dancers, amateurs, seasoned contact improvisers and beginners, people from all backgrounds and abilities. It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. Event page: https://millco.co.uk/events/contact-improvisation-jam/ https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-scnfy-20260601183000

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1+2 (Course of 11 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 (Beginners 1) And Mondays 01/06, 08/06, 15/06, 22/06, 29/06 and 06/07 (Beginners 2) from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. Beginners 1: The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. Beginners 2: It will build on what we started in Beginners 1, deepening your understanding of the basics and developing more vocabulary for giving and receiving weight, moving in close connection with the floor, rolling and falling. We will work on expanding confidence in: Expressing what you want and do not want in your partner dances Creativity and playfulness Starting and finishing dances Deep physical listening Dancing in trios Lifting and being lifted Jamming skills I will be working with new material, so it will be a way of revisiting the fundamentals while learning new pathways. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-smfda-20260601183000

sessions.title: ROCKET
sessions.details: Rocket is deeply rooted in Ashtanga. It is a series of standing, balancing and inverted postures all linked by vinyasas (movement flows), incorporating basic poses with challenging arm balances, inversions and back bends Inversions are lot of fun, but they also prove to be some of the most challenging postures. Some of the upside down postures are designed to energise us, others are designed to calm us down. No matter if you are a newbie or an old hat to inversions this class will be fun, will get you sweating and see the world from another perspective -upside down.

sessions.title: Professional Class
sessions.details: *Please note, professional class now runs from Tuesday to Thursday (8:00am-9:30am). Our daily classes for professional-level dancers are led each week by a different artist from the international dance community. Each teacher brings their own style and technique to class, from their experience performing with world-leading dance companies and choreographers. With a strong focus on honing and maintaining technique, you’ll be challenged and inspired amongst peers. Professional class is ‘drop in’ and be booked by the day. sessions.title: Contemporary for Over 60s
sessions.details: In this Contemporary class, you’ll be developing your contemporary technique while also learning some new moves – taking inspiration from a variety of traditional Caribbean dances. You will be able to create and play with those moves in a variety of ways. This class features a live musician. Led by Rambert faculty member Paradigmz. He’s worked alongside choreographers across contemporary and classical African Peoples Dance, as well Jazz and Hip Hop and Modern Dance Forms and offers extensive experience. Artists and companies include Sakoba Dance Theatre, Jackie Guy, (Norman Rubber) Stephenson and many more. Building Information Classes take place at Rambert, 99 Upper Ground SE1 9PP. We have a fully accessible building, including accessible toilets and showers. There is on-street parking for Blue Badge holders with step-free access to the building, and lifts to all levels. Changing facilities are available on the first floor. A water fountain is available on the second floor- please bring your own reuse-able bottle for this. You can wear whatever your are comfortable moving in, and you’re welcome to wear dance shoes if you have them (although no dark/black soles) or bare-feet. Please make sure you have removed jewellery before class, and long hair is tied back. Please note, as the studios are used by our professional dancers we ask that you refrain from using hair products and body lotions as these can make the floor slippery. Terms and Conditions of Booking If you need to cancel your booking, you can do so up to 48 hours before a drop in and up to 48 hours before the first class of a term booking for a full refund in class credits by logging into your Momence account. If you'd prefer a monetary refund, just email us to let us know.

sessions.title: Rueda Libre Wednesday
sessions.details: Coal Drops Yard, Coal Drops Yard, King's Cross, London, N1C 4DQ, United Kingdom • Join Us for an Unforgettable Outdoor Cuban Salsa Event! Get ready to dance, learn, meet amazing people, and embrace the joy of salsa dancing! Our outdoor salsa event is the perfect place to spice up your evening, whether you’re a seasoned pro or have never danced a step in your life. Here’s what to expect: Cuban Salsa and Rueda Classes: We’re offering classes for all levels, from absolute beginners to advanced dancers. No partner? No problem! Everyone is welcome to join in the fun. Visit https://ruedalibre.co.uk/classes/ to find out which class level suits you best. Class Time: Classes kick off at 7:00 PM, but make sure to arrive by 6:45 PM to show your QR code and collect your wristband. This ensures you’re ready and wont miss the beginning of the class. Free Outdoor Social Dancing: After the class, the night doesn’t end! Stick around for some free outdoor social dancing. Practice your moves, connect with the community, and just let loose. The vibe is 10/10 so enjoy it. Affordable Pricing: Classes start at just £9 (excluding fees), and you’ll have the chance to practice what you’ve learned during the session. The most budget-friendly way to pay is via our QR code in person, no fees to worry about. Prefer other options? We also accept cash, contactless payments, and online payments for your convenience. Whether you’re a salsa enthusiast or simply looking for a new experience, this is your chance to dance, laugh, and create unforgettable memories. Join us and make the most of your Wednesday evening. Ready to dance? Grab your spot and let’s make this a night to remember. See you there!

sessions.title: Wednesday Moving - Franziska Boehm
sessions.details: Round Chapel Old School Rooms, Powerscroft Road, Hackney E5 0PU • Franzi, a German movement artist, performative researcher and teacher in London, takes great joy in integrating her musical background into her movement work. "I sing a sound which could become a melody, a process of sensing, or a movement". Franzi's session will draw on Skinner Releasing Technique (SRT) - using poetic imagery, supportive music and guided touch - to engage in movement and sound improvisation.

sessions.title: Playfulness for Beginners (4-week course)
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • 7.15-9.00pm on Wednesdays June 3rd, 10th, 17th and 24thWho says your spiritual practice needs to be serious? What if playfulness could become a pathway towards self-discovery and wholeness?Come and join us for this 4-week introductory ‘practice of playfulness' journey, where grown up adults can reconnect with their often buried sense of childlike play. We will draw from the worlds of clowning, improv, mime and dance as well as spontaneous silliness and generalised irreverence. Together, this unlikely cocktail will leave you feeling joyous, open-hearted and flooded with endorphins.Through a range of games and structures, we will explore aspects of play such as spontaneity, misbehaviour, exuberance, sensitivity, connection and totality - and also take time to explore and process how we are feeling as we undergo the journey.The workshops will be a safe space with no pressure ‘to perform’- although the urge may arise. Rather the aim is to build an encouraging supportive nest from which you can launch yourself into your innately exuberant and playful aspect and free your inner child.Some aspects of the workshop will be held and structured, others will be a little bit free and spontaneous (and even occasionally anarchic), all interspersed with dancing and 'digestion time.' There will also be a chill-out area should you need to sit things out for a while ************* During this course you will: Discover how The Practice of Playfulness is a healing medicine that can transform emotions such as repression, numbness and disconnection into feelings of happiness, optimism and inner aliveness.See how the path of self-expression develops inner qualities such as courage, creativity, confidence and improved communication skills.Understand how play gives a strong taste of emotional freedom and moment-by-moment living in a real, embodied way.Be supported through regular sharing circles and times for self-reflection. ************* Read other people's experience of the course:“I believe that what Ailon is offering is incredibly powerful and if you want to live life with a bit more lightheartedness then you should definitely go along to his workshops!”“Thank you for an enriching and ridiculous 6 weeks of playfulness.I loved the journey and cultivating the trust to play together allowed fresh and unexpected expressions to emerge.”“For me this is less of a class or workshop and more of a happening…a congregation of joyful souls happy to hang out and relax in a climate of friendliness. Out of that trust, true silliness and fun can emerge.”“Thank you for bringing into fruition a space which is so playful and nourishing to the soul. To have all our parts to come up and be met, not only with with encouragement but with love is so rare in this world- it takes weird and deep to awaken and meet weird and deep!”“ It’s been a pleasure being on this journey with every single one of you and see everyone expand and grow on this journey into deeper expression of our selves. I appreciate everyone’s acceptance and kindness. It’s been the first place in a long time where I felt safe and accepted to just be myself and explore parts of myself no matter how crazy, silly and unexpected.”"Ailon creates such a safe and humorous space for people to explore their inner joker and let go of their inhibitions. I’ve given myself permission to be playful again and it’s been so liberating to reconnect with that part of me."“What a pleasure and a privilege to be part of this workshop” “Like being drunk with no alcohol”****************They can't all be wrong ???Any questions email: ailon@schoolofplayfulness.co.ukTo read more about Ailon (the founder)'s journey into playfulness have a look herehttps://ailonfreedman.substack.com/p/birthing-the-school-of-playfulness7.15-9.00pm on Wednesdays June 3rd, 10th, 17th and 24thWho says your spiritual practice needs to be serious? sessions.title: ProDance class with Marla King
sessions.details: The class will weave through guided improvisation and structured movement sequences, with the aim of awakening our sequentiality, a sense of flow in the body, and expanding the qualities, sensations and possibilities that feel open to us in our dancing. A space to be playful, engage our imagination, welcome challenge, follow what lights us up, and nurture our connection with one another. Exploring and experiencing the strength and power that is held in softness and sensitivity. Expect a sweaty, spirally, wavy, connective morning with ecology-inspired movement explorations and some wholesome music!

sessions.title: LATIN-FUSION DANCE
sessions.details: A joyful, high-energy class blending Latin dance styles with contemporary movement and expressive flow. In this 60-minute session, you’ll explore rhythm, musicality, and full-body movement through accessible choreography and playful combinations. Open to all levels, the class offers options and variations so you can move at your own pace—whether you’re new to dance or looking to deepen your groove. Expect a supportive atmosphere, a good sweat, and plenty of space to connect with the music, your body, and the joy of movement. No partner needed. Come as you are, leave energised and inspired.

sessions.details: Instructor: Rowan Hicks | Level: All | Room: Studio 2 | Location: In Studio Classes | The perfect class for beginners or those looking to kick-start their day with a signature warm up and stretch grounded in dance technique. sessions.details: Instructor: David Kierce | Level: Beg | Room: Studio 11 | Location: In Studio Classes | Absolute beginners is for anybody brand new to ballet - we start from the beginning; the correct posture, and the basic positions of the arms and legs. The class is about how your body moves naturally in everyday life and how that natural movement transfers to ballet. You will also learn how to move in time and to the rhythm of the music. There is a joyful and light-hearted atmosphere - newcomers are welcome at any time and they fit in easily to the flow of the class.

sessions.title: Tap - Beginner Tap (Abs Beg/Adv Beg) £13 Beaux
sessions.details: Instructor: Beaux Harris | Level: Beg | Room: Studio 2 | Location: In Studio Classes | This BEGINNER TAP class is open and catered to all levels of Beginner (those who have never Tapped before and want to learn a new skill *OR* for those who have done a little and want to brush up their technique). Together we will cover all of the TAP basics, dancing to the greatest hits in a safe and uplifting environment. Your little one's are welcome! We will begin with a relaxed ‘follow me’ warm up, leading onto some centre work, basic travelling sequences & then finish with a fun routine which I will switch up every 2 weeks. Come & connect with your inner child, re discover the joy in creating rhythms, move your gorgeous body & celebrate this unique and special art form with me. This class will be available to stream via ZOOM for any one who can’t attend in person. Follow @movewithbeaux for all weekly class updates.

sessions.title: Street Dance/Commercial - Commercial (Int/16+) £13 Poppy Radford
sessions.details: Instructor: Poppy Radford | Level: Int | Room: Studio 2 | Location: In Studio Classes | This intermediate class is all about challenging, full-out choreography that’s fast-paced and genuinely fun. We’ll focus on quicker pick-up, dynamics, and performance, while keeping the environment supportive and encouraging. It is a safe space where you can push yourself, make mistakes, and grow without pressure. Big energy and good vibes are a must! You’ll leave the room feeling confident, empowered, and like an absolute baddie.

sessions.title: Tap - Tap (Int) £13 Mike Denman
sessions.details: Instructor: Mike Denman | Level: Int | Room: Studio 6 | Location: In Studio Classes | Designed for dancers with a good foundation in tap, this fun and energetic class builds on different styles while developing cleaner technique, sharper rhythms and lively choreography.

sessions.title: Ballet - Ballet (Adv/Pro) £13 Adam
sessions.details: Instructor: Adam Pudney | Level: Adv/Pro | Room: Studio 11 | Location: In Studio Classes | Adam’s Advanced/Professional classes will test the brain as well as the body, thereby ensuring dancers who know their way around a ballet class have to remain switched on, rather than just going through the motions on autopilot.Expect the unexpected! He incorporates these performance elements into the training of aspiring and accomplished dancers so that they are equipped with all the necessary tools for auditions and ultimately, the stage.

sessions.details: Instructor: Avalon Rathgeb/Old Kent Rd | Level: Int/Adv | Room: Studio 5 | Location: In Studio Classes | This class is for the Intermediate/Advanced tap dancer that has a high standard of knowledge and understanding of all fundamental steps and musical ideas. sessions.title: Playfulness for Beginners (4-week course)
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • 7.15-9.00pm on Wednesdays June 3rd, 10th, 17th and 24thWho says your spiritual practice needs to be serious? What if playfulness could become a pathway towards self-discovery and wholeness?Come and join us for this 4-week introductory ‘practice of playfulness' journey, where grown up adults can reconnect with their often buried sense of childlike play. We will draw from the worlds of clowning, improv, mime and dance as well as spontaneous silliness and generalised irreverence. sessions.title: Baduanjin Qigong (8-week course)
sessions.details: Colet House, 151 Talgarth Rd, London W14 9DA • BADUANJIN QIGONG – The Eight Silk BrocadesAn Eight-Week Qigong Course with Natalia Miralles Huete📅 Course dates: 8 classes from 9 April to 4 June (No class on 23 April)18:30 – 19:30📍 Location: Top Studio, Colet HouseBaduanjin, also known as “The Eight Silk Brocades”, is an ancient Qigong set of eight different fluid movements that together condition the whole body externally — stretching and strengthening it — and internally, improving the function of the organs and systems (respiratory, circulatory, digestive, nervous, etc.).The set was first described in an eighth-century Taoist text, and it is known to have been used effectively throughout the 17th century during wars in China to alleviate soldiers’ fatigue. This is a key aspect of Qigong, as it helps us to regain energy and vitality to go about our modern daily lives and face our inner battles of stress and emotional challenges.Baduanjin represents an excellent short daily health routine. It will provide you with a whole-body workout, mobilising all your joints, strengthening your muscles and bones, and improving your posture and balance, while helping to focus and calm your busy mind. Your emotions will also feel more balanced, and your energy levels will increase.Once you have learnt the set, it will take you just 20 minutes to complete, although the practice can be shorter or longer depending on the number of repetitions. If you persevere in practising the set daily or a few times per week after the course, you will soon notice the health benefits it brings.The course also includes the essential foundations for effective Qigong practice: breathing techniques, preparatory self-massage, structured joint-opening exercises, and the “three regulations” — body, breath and mind — providing a clear and methodical framework for practising Baduanjin safely and efficiently.BADUANJIN QIGONG – The Eight Silk BrocadesAn Eight-Week Qigong Course with Natalia Miralles Huete📅 Course dates: 8 classes from 9 April to 4 June (No class on 23 April)18:30 – 19:30📍 Location: Top Studio, Colet HouseBaduanjin, also known as “The Eight Silk Brocades”, is an ancient Qigong set of eight different fluid movements that together condition the whole body externally — stretching and strengthening it — and internally, improving the function of the organs and systems (respiratory, circulatory, digestive, nervous, etc.).The set was first described in an eighth-century Taoist text, and it is known to have been used effectively throughout the 17th century during wars in China to alleviate soldiers’ fatigue. sessions.title: Countertechnique class &  Physical Theatre WORKSHOP
sessions.details: This dynamic workshop with Borna Babić begins with a Countertechnique class, focusing on efficiency, clarity, and expanding movement possibilities through the organisation of the body in space. Participants will work with tools that enhance coordination, awareness, and availability for movement, building both physical stamina and adaptability. The second half of the workshop shifts into physical theatre exploration, investigating the connection between intention, emotion, and movement. Through guided improvisation tasks and playful games, participants will be encouraged to deepen their individuality and discover how their personal impulses can inform performance. We will explore two equally valuable approaches within the creative process: allowing physicality to evoke intention and emotion, and embodying thought or emotional states to generate movement. Particular attention will be given to researching different physical qualities and textures, and how these can be integrated into partnering work. In an open, supportive, and curious environment, we will challenge habitual movement patterns and cultivate sensitivity to detail, authenticity, and performative presence.

sessions.title: Saturday CI x Aikido Workshop with Rosalie Wahlfrid: The Power of Letting Go
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • In this workshop, we will explore the potential of the quiet body. Through movement and meditative practices, we will investigate how qualities such as softening, absorbing and deflecting may generate power, efficiency and responsiveness in movement. The workshop will introduce simple Aikido techniques alongside the fundamentals of posture and embodiment in Aikido and explore physical and mental states such as spatial awareness and internal focus. We will consider how these principles and techniques may support more fluid and responsive interactions in Contact Improvisation, while expanding our shared movement vocabulary. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-sfc76-20260606143000

sessions.title: Gaga People
sessions.details: Gaga is the movement language developed by Ohad Naharin throughout many years, parallel to his work as a choreographer and artistic director (1990-2018) of Batsheva Dance Company. Gaga originated from Naharin’s need to communicate with his dancers and his curiosity in the ongoing research of movement. Gaga classes are predicated on a deep listening to the body and to physical sensations. The instructions are deployed to increase awareness of and further amplify sensation, and rather than turning from one prompt to another, information is layered, building into a multisensory, physically challenging experience. While many instructions are imbued with rich imagery, the research of Gaga is fundamentally physical, insisting on a specific process of embodiment. Inside this shared research, the improvisational nature of the exploration enables each participant’s deeply personal connection with Gaga. Throughout the class, participants are guided by a series of evocative instructions deployed to increase awareness of and further amplify sensation. Rather than turning from one prompt to another, information is layered, building into a multisensory, physically challenging experience. While many instructions are imbued with rich imagery, the research of Gaga is fundamentally physical, insisting on a specific process of embodiment. Inside this shared research, the improvisational nature of the exploration enables each participant’s deeply personal connection with Gaga. Participants should wear comfortable clothes and be prepared to dance barefoot or in socks. It is advisable to bring a bottle of water and a towel for use after class.

Rather than turning from one prompt to another, information is layered, building into a multisensory, physically challenging experience. sessions.title: THE ARC OF ATTENTION CI Class with Justin Philpott & Jam Soundscape by Carlo Natoli
sessions.details: Room 154, Richard Hoggart Building, Goldsmiths, Lewisham Way, London, SE14 6NW • A two hour Contact Improvisation class starting at 13:00 class followed by a jam at 15:00 finishing at 18:00. THE ARC OF ATTENTION This class explores circular movement as a pathway into contact improvisation. Beginning in stillness, we gently notice the journey of our awareness as we flow into self-led movement. From there, we explore circles, arcs and spirals through the body, allowing rolling, curving and looping pathways to emerge through improvisation. From this solo exploration, we gradually move into relation: first dancing with an awareness of others from a distance, then drawing closer, and eventually finding touch. We will then practise the skill of projecting from the ground, through the centre, and towards the point of contact with each other. With this experience in place, we return to circular movement and explore how contact becomes clearer: how we attend, meet, support and move with another through a shared point of connection. From there, the class opens naturally into the jam. About Justin: Justin is the host and resident teacher of the Brighton CI Community. He is a multidisciplinary mover with a background in martial arts and Thai-style bodywork. He has been dancing CI for over 12 years, teaching CI since 2018, and runs Moving Stillness - School of Somatics (https://www.moving-stillness.com). See the website for more details on our pricing tiers. CLASS DESCRIPTION This class will follow the traditional structure of the codified technique, sequencing through a set series of seated floor exercises, standing exercises and across-the-floor sequences. The Graham Technique is an immensely valuable technique to layer on top of any dance training as it emphasises the importance of the usage of the back, as well as accessing the deep core abdominal muscles.Fundamental principles in Graham Technique are the contraction and release, opposition, shift of weight and spirals. Graham dancers believe that it is important that we not simply see ourselves as objects in space when dancing, but that we expand their body, energy and focus so they are amplified enough to fill that space. The class will serve to free up the back, open up the hips and the body. On top, form the dancer to find dynamics, intricacy and articulation of the spine. Minimum age: 16

sessions.title: ProDance Class with Billy Maxwell-Taylor
sessions.details: Through improvisation, crossings, and a focus on spaciousness, this class invites the interplay of tranquility and vitality - the humming energy of the body. How can we move without judgement and with deep listening? Underscored by ambient music and a touch of bubbly jazz, this space offers an opportunity to ground into our dance practice while developing our physical foundations through mobilization, soft core stabilization and meditation. Expect invitations like "take time", "notice" and "ride the joy of this disappearing moment".

sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. Suitable for most levels, this class is a beautiful way to care for your body, move more freely, and give yourself the reset you didn’t know you needed.

sessions.title: YANG TO YIN
sessions.details: This class will flow through the energies of Yang into Yin. The first half will be focused on dynamic vinyasa-style asana to connect with and work the physical body through strong postures, an awareness of breath, a deep connection to sensation and body-mindfulness. The second half is designed to stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system with long floor-based postures, supported by meditation and mindfulness techniques to calm, ground and reset. ***Please note: Booking window for Online classes closes 30 minutes before class starts.

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1+2 (Course of 11 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 (Beginners 1) And Mondays 01/06, 08/06, 15/06, 22/06, 29/06 and 06/07 (Beginners 2) from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. Beginners 1: The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. Beginners 2: It will build on what we started in Beginners 1, deepening your understanding of the basics and developing more vocabulary for giving and receiving weight, moving in close connection with the floor, rolling and falling. We will work on expanding confidence in: Expressing what you want and do not want in your partner dances Creativity and playfulness Starting and finishing dances Deep physical listening Dancing in trios Lifting and being lifted Jamming skills I will be working with new material, so it will be a way of revisiting the fundamentals while learning new pathways. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-smfda-20260608183000

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1+2 (Course of 11 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 (Beginners 1) And Mondays 01/06, 08/06, 15/06, 22/06, 29/06 and 06/07 (Beginners 2) from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. Beginners 1: The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. Beginners 2: It will build on what we started in Beginners 1, deepening your understanding of the basics and developing more vocabulary for giving and receiving weight, moving in close connection with the floor, rolling and falling. We will work on expanding confidence in: Expressing what you want and do not want in your partner dances Creativity and playfulness Starting and finishing dances Deep physical listening Dancing in trios Lifting and being lifted Jamming skills I will be working with new material, so it will be a way of revisiting the fundamentals while learning new pathways. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-smfda-20260608183000
