sessions.title: ProDance class with Justin De Jager & Tia Hockey
sessions.details: In this class Justin and Tia will share elements of their current research of a hybrid movement approach, exploring an instinctive fusion of threading and contact improvisation/partnering. Threading’s precise, spatial geometry and entangling puzzles are integrated with contact improvisation’s weight-sharing dialogue and tactile negotiation. To begin, we will establish a shared understanding of chosen threading concepts through physicalised tools and concept-based tasks. This exploration will lead into the partnering aspect of the language, building our kinaesthetic awareness, activating embodied problem-solving skills and encouraging creative freedom through a guided improvisational practice. Photo: Jack Thomson

sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. Suitable for most levels, this class is a beautiful way to care for your body, move more freely, and give yourself the reset you didn’t know you needed.

sessions.title: YANG TO YIN
sessions.details: This class will flow through the energies of Yang into Yin. The first half will be focused on dynamic vinyasa-style asana to connect with and work the physical body through strong postures, an awareness of breath, a deep connection to sensation and body-mindfulness. The second half is designed to stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system with long floor-based postures, supported by meditation and mindfulness techniques to calm, ground and reset. ***Please note: Booking window for Online classes closes 30 minutes before class starts.

sessions.details: Laban Building • Creekside, London, SE8 3DZ, UK, London • This women-only stretch class is a highly requested add-on for anyone who wants a low-pressure space dedicated entirely to stretching. It is not yoga. Instead, it is a guided group fitness session built to improve flexibility, mobility and range of motion through focused, full-body stretching techniques. By the end of the session, you should feel physically lighter, taller, more open and less stiff, with a calmer mind and a stronger sense of connection to your body. Because stretching time is often overlooked in busy schedules, this class creates a rare space where you can slow down, move with care, and leave feeling both released and re-energised. Who it’s for Women who want a calm, private, and comfortable space to stretch. Women who want to improve flexibility, mobility and range of motion. Women who prefer a guided stretch session rather than yoga. Women who want time to release tension and reset. What to expect You will move through a guided stretch and mobility session that combines careful, full-body work with space to breathe, release and settle into the room. The pace is controlled, supportive and focused on making the body feel more open and available. Every ticket includes a goody bag. Outcome You leave feeling looser, freer, more open through the body and more mentally settled. Practical note Please arrive 10–15 minutes early so you can settle in and get familiar with the space before class begins. If you are pregnant, postnatal, or managing an injury, please let the team know in advance so adjustments can be made. What to Wear Anything you feel comfortable in and able to stretch freely. This class is 18+ only. By purchasing a ticket, you agree to these terms and conditions.

sessions.title: Monday Beginners Level 1+2 (Course of 11 classes)
sessions.details: Acland Burghley School Sports Centre, Churchill Road, London, NW5 1AN • Mondays 27/04, 04/05, 11/05, 18/05 and 25/05 (Beginners 1) And Mondays 01/06, 08/06, 15/06, 22/06, 29/06 and 06/07 (Beginners 2) from 6:30 to 8:30pm. Classes taught by Rick Nodine. Beginners 1: The course is a carefully crafted syllabus that will support beginners in understanding the conceptual and physical world of Contact Improvisation (CI) so that they can trust their own opinions about what they want as they dive into the CI experience. Connecting with other people is at the core of this practice and you will learn how CI roots connection in the reality of touch and movement. Class 1) A talk about what CI is and what to expect from it, a lead somatic warm-up and a solo physical exploration about moving comfortably in close connection with the floor, exercises about communicating with a partner through touch and physical listening, discussion of consensual touch and freedom of choice in dancing, a space for questions and concerns to be expressed and addressed. Class 2) We will learn some simple patterns that open different body surfaces to meeting in contact. Exercises that clarify how to get in and out of dances will strengthen your agency in following your interests within a group. Class 3) Exercises about exchanging body weight with a partner will be the beginning of the thrill of taking risks, understanding that good communication leads to pleasure in weight exchange and a lack of communication leads to discomfort, feeling your strength and understanding your limits. Class 4) Exercises about how to fall safely, learning more CI vocabulary to expand possibilities in physical communication, building confidence in starting and ending dances. Class 5) Understanding Jamming and how to decode its rules and etiquette, responses to specific questions and a discussion about transitioning to open classes and jams. Integrating previous learning into free dancing and connecting to fun and risk in movement. Beginners 2: It will build on what we started in Beginners 1, deepening your understanding of the basics and developing more vocabulary for giving and receiving weight, moving in close connection with the floor, rolling and falling. We will work on expanding confidence in: Expressing what you want and do not want in your partner dances Creativity and playfulness Starting and finishing dances Deep physical listening Dancing in trios Lifting and being lifted Jamming skills I will be working with new material, so it will be a way of revisiting the fundamentals while learning new pathways. https://bookwhen.com/ricknodine/e/ev-smfda-20260706183000

sessions.title: Monday Contact Improv: Class + Jam
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 5SQ • Doors open at 6.20pm Please note they won't be an intro circle anymore. First timers can arrive a bit earlier for any questions and info around consent or about the jam. I also advise newcomers to familiarise themselves with the guidelines. This week we have a class taught by Marie, an experienced CI practitioner (22 years), professional dancer and choreographer. Theme and Content The theme of the class will be posted closer to the time in the CI Monday Jam WhatsApp group. You can join in following this link: https://chat.whatsapp.com/Iivbz8LzDvK5lGkiitQgcH (please note I will ask you a few question about yourself before I allow you into the chat, when you join please introduce yourself so we know who's in the chat) These Contact Improvisation classes give participants tools to be in touch and communicate through touch, and feel more confident joining a jam. There are open levels and benefit beginners, improvers and experienced practitioners. There is a mix of somatic guided exploration to be embodied, usually in solo, some mindful and focused explorations with one or several partners, and some more technical tools or short patterns. This will be followed by a 45min-1h jam Jam The emphasis of the jam is to explore movement while being in physical contact with other movers. Participants are encouraged to experience it as an embodied research and a practice where everyone can bring their own research, interest and physicality into the space. Jamming is the best way to try out, take risks, learn from each other, observe, connect, be surprised, practice setting boundaries, dance and play with people we may not know or expect to dance with. Participants are asked to take responsibility for themselves. Levels and abilities: The space welcomes professional dancers, amateurs, seasoned contact improvisers and beginners, people from all backgrounds and abilities. It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. Event page: https://millco.co.uk/events/contact-improvisation-jam/ https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-sqjez-20260706183000

sessions.title: ProDance class with Justin De Jager & Tia Hockey
sessions.details: In this class Justin and Tia will share elements of their current research of a hybrid movement approach, exploring an instinctive fusion of threading and contact improvisation/partnering. Threading’s precise, spatial geometry and entangling puzzles are integrated with contact improvisation’s weight-sharing dialogue and tactile negotiation. To begin, we will establish a shared understanding of chosen threading concepts through physicalised tools and concept-based tasks. This exploration will lead into the partnering aspect of the language, building our kinaesthetic awareness, activating embodied problem-solving skills and encouraging creative freedom through a guided improvisational practice. sessions.title: ROCKET
sessions.details: Rocket is deeply rooted in Ashtanga. It is a series of standing, balancing and inverted postures all linked by vinyasas (movement flows), incorporating basic poses with challenging arm balances, inversions and back bends Inversions are lot of fun, but they also prove to be some of the most challenging postures. Some of the upside down postures are designed to energise us, others are designed to calm us down. No matter if you are a newbie or an old hat to inversions this class will be fun, will get you sweating and see the world from another perspective -upside down.

sessions.title: ProDance class with Justin De Jager & Tia Hockey
sessions.details: In this class Justin and Tia will share elements of their current research of a hybrid movement approach, exploring an instinctive fusion of threading and contact improvisation/partnering. Threading’s precise, spatial geometry and entangling puzzles are integrated with contact improvisation’s weight-sharing dialogue and tactile negotiation. To begin, we will establish a shared understanding of chosen threading concepts through physicalised tools and concept-based tasks. This exploration will lead into the partnering aspect of the language, building our kinaesthetic awareness, activating embodied problem-solving skills and encouraging creative freedom through a guided improvisational practice. Photo: Jack Thomson

CLASS DESCRIPTION: Do you want to limit your injury risk, while also building strength to become a better dancer? This fitness class will help you substantially improve your posture and correct any issues relating to your body alignment. It is very easy to create bad habits in ballet, so changing these habits often requires retraining muscle memory. Christina's Posture Power with PBT elements class will not only help you build up more strength and flexibility, but will also help you train the muscle memory required for automatically performing movements the right way. This class will be accompanied by music. With her experience as a coach, ballet teacher and approved PBT instructor, Christina has put together a class that will help you limit your injury risk and become a stronger and better dancer. Posture Power with PBT elements is a general level class and therefore suitable for those, who either wish to improve their ballet technique or simply improve their fitness level. It is also a perfect preparation for her 11:30 Int/Adv ballet class which takes place right after her Posture Power with PBT elements class. Progressing Ballet Technique (PBT) is an innovative programme which was developed by Marie Walton- Mahon in order to help dancers and students improve their technique. The programme includes carefully designed exercises focusing on training muscle memory and improving core strength, weight placement and alignment of the body. Minimum age: 14

sessions.title: ProDance class with Justin De Jager & Tia Hockey
sessions.details: In this class Justin and Tia will share elements of their current research of a hybrid movement approach, exploring an instinctive fusion of threading and contact improvisation/partnering. Threading’s precise, spatial geometry and entangling puzzles are integrated with contact improvisation’s weight-sharing dialogue and tactile negotiation. To begin, we will establish a shared understanding of chosen threading concepts through physicalised tools and concept-based tasks. This exploration will lead into the partnering aspect of the language, building our kinaesthetic awareness, activating embodied problem-solving skills and encouraging creative freedom through a guided improvisational practice. sessions.title: Gaga People
sessions.details: Gaga is the movement language developed by Ohad Naharin throughout many years, parallel to his work as a choreographer and artistic director (1990-2018) of Batsheva Dance Company. Gaga originated from Naharin’s need to communicate with his dancers and his curiosity in the ongoing research of movement. Gaga classes are predicated on a deep listening to the body and to physical sensations. The instructions are deployed to increase awareness of and further amplify sensation, and rather than turning from one prompt to another, information is layered, building into a multisensory, physically challenging experience. While many instructions are imbued with rich imagery, the research of Gaga is fundamentally physical, insisting on a specific process of embodiment. Inside this shared research, the improvisational nature of the exploration enables each participant’s deeply personal connection with Gaga. Throughout the class, participants are guided by a series of evocative instructions deployed to increase awareness of and further amplify sensation. Rather than turning from one prompt to another, information is layered, building into a multisensory, physically challenging experience. While many instructions are imbued with rich imagery, the research of Gaga is fundamentally physical, insisting on a specific process of embodiment. Inside this shared research, the improvisational nature of the exploration enables each participant’s deeply personal connection with Gaga. Participants should wear comfortable clothes and be prepared to dance barefoot or in socks. It is advisable to bring a bottle of water and a towel for use after class.

sessions.title: **Women’s Touch : Community as a relational process - workshop lab**
sessions.details: Siobhan Davies Studios, 85 Saint George's Road, London, SE1 6ER • Embodiment - Community - Develop self-enquiry and agency- Be in touch - Share reflection + Experiences + Food After the great success and feedback from the last Women's Touch event, I've decided to put together another one to follow-up on this inspiring and rich theme of Community as a relational process. What's different from the last one? More lab time, more time to co-create, journal and share impressions. We won't use yarns this time around but a different material... I'll reveal it later. What is it? Marie will facilitate this Contact Impro workshop/laboratory exploring how community forms through relation and difference. Weaving between movement scores and moments of shared reflection, participants are invited to experience connection in and out of contact. We will open up questions and investigations such as: -How do I enter and inhabit a group? -What helps me feel connected without erasing difference? -Is community something we belong to, or something we continuously make? Work unfolds through solo and group scores, supporting attentive connection, experimentation, and self-enquiry. The space intends to be safe, consent-based, and accessible to all. Rough schedule (may change slightly) 11.30am-12pm – Welcome tea & chat (meeting each other + time & space to land) 12pm –1.30pm – Intro to Consent, solo warm-up and collective embodied explorations 1.30-2.30pm – Lunchtime: food sharing 2.30-5.30pm – Group scores Small group reflection: community as a relational process Witnessing, writing, sharing and integrating Who is this for? Those who identify as women and non-binary interested in bringing more awareness to physical interactions in dancing and in Contact Improvisation It welcomes all levels and can be applied to other practices than Contact Improvisation. In the past people were able to apply it to dance therapy, theatre, psychology... This lab is open level. No prior experience of Contact Improv is required What is Women's Touch? Women’s touch is an event curated by Marie Chabert, that offers a space for those who identify as women and non-binary to explore movement practices that are mainly based on touch (Contact Improvisation, somatic practices, improvisation) in a safe environment. It aims to empower women to claim their space and redefine it within a framework that challenges prevailing patriarchal norms. It offers both a place to embody and share our experiences verbally. The intention is to foster a supportive environment, where participants feel safe to take risks, be vulnerable, and share their humanity, free from the pressure of dominant dynamics. Cultivating such spaces requires trust, shared language, and mutual care. It allows us not just to survive, but to thrive in connection. If you have financial difficulties and want to take part, please get in touch. photo by Sol Ji Park https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-sq6op-20260712113000

CLASS DESCRIPTION: Do you want to limit your injury risk, while also building strength to become a better dancer? This fitness class will help you substantially improve your posture and correct any issues relating to your body alignment. It is very easy to create bad habits in ballet, so changing these habits often requires retraining muscle memory. Christina's Posture Power with PBT elements class will not only help you build up more strength and flexibility, but will also help you train the muscle memory required for automatically performing movements the right way. This class will be accompanied by music. With her experience as a coach, ballet teacher and approved PBT instructor, Christina has put together a class that will help you limit your injury risk and become a stronger and better dancer. Posture Power with PBT elements is a general level class and therefore suitable for those, who either wish to improve their ballet technique or simply improve their fitness level. It is also a perfect preparation for her 11:30 Int/Adv ballet class which takes place right after her Posture Power with PBT elements class. Progressing Ballet Technique (PBT) is an innovative programme which was developed by Marie Walton- Mahon in order to help dancers and students improve their technique. The programme includes carefully designed exercises focusing on training muscle memory and improving core strength, weight placement and alignment of the body. Minimum age: 14

CLASS DESCRIPTION This class will follow the traditional structure of the codified technique, sequencing through a set series of seated floor exercises, standing exercises and across-the-floor sequences. The Graham Technique is an immensely valuable technique to layer on top of any dance training as it emphasises the importance of the usage of the back, as well as accessing the deep core abdominal muscles.Fundamental principles in Graham Technique are the contraction and release, opposition, shift of weight and spirals. Graham dancers believe that it is important that we not simply see ourselves as objects in space when dancing, but that we expand their body, energy and focus so they are amplified enough to fill that space. The class will serve to free up the back, open up the hips and the body. On top, form the dancer to find dynamics, intricacy and articulation of the spine. Minimum age: 16

sessions.title: ProDance Class with Kieran Brown
sessions.details: 'A release-based class cultivating awareness through movement. The class aims to develop softness and somatic presence through form, playing with weight and flow to expand and inhabit our dancing bodies through space. We begin on the floor, guided by principles of Feldenkrais to build somatic awareness and awaken the body’s intelligence. Through gentle, intentional exploration of the skeletal structure, attuning to sensation, gradually building heat and structure as we make our way to standing. From this grounded foundation, we transition into improvised crossings, activating the senses through touch. We explore the body’s relationship to gravity—playing with the weight of the limbs, head, and pelvis, and riding the architecture of the body from within. As the class progresses, we learn set material, approaching it with an improvisational sensibility. Inviting this into choreographed phrases that explore soft expansion and length, playing with weight transference and coordination through space.’

sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. Suitable for most levels, this class is a beautiful way to care for your body, move more freely, and give yourself the reset you didn’t know you needed.

sessions.title: YANG TO YIN
sessions.details: This class will flow through the energies of Yang into Yin. The first half will be focused on dynamic vinyasa-style asana to connect with and work the physical body through strong postures, an awareness of breath, a deep connection to sensation and body-mindfulness. The second half is designed to stimulate the parasympathetic nervous system with long floor-based postures, supported by meditation and mindfulness techniques to calm, ground and reset. ***Please note: Booking window for Online classes closes 30 minutes before class starts.

sessions.title: Monday Contact Improv Jam : dress-up jam @centre 151
sessions.details: Centre 151, 151 Whiston Road, London, E2 8GU • Doors open at 6.20pm Please note they won't be an intro circle anymore. First timers can arrive a bit earlier for any questions and info around consent or about the jam. I also advise newcomers to familiarise themselves with the guidelines. This weekly jam invites movers to jam together for a regular practice. Warming-up: Marie Chabert will facilitate the warming-up before the jam. The aim is for participants to arrive into their body, tune in, connect to themselves, to others and to the space around. It brings people into their senses and embodied awareness. It is not a class and doesn't give the same technical tools and principles as a class. Classes are held every other week and will give you these skills. Jam The emphasis of the jam is to explore movement while being in physical contact with other movers. Participants are encouraged to experience it as an embodied research and a practice where everyone can bring their own research, interest and physicality into the space. Jamming is the best way to try out, take risks, learn from each other, observe, connect, be surprised, practice setting boundaries, dance and play with people we may not know or expect to dance with. Participants are asked to take responsibility for themselves. Levels and abilities: The space welcomes professional dancers, amateurs, seasoned contact improvisers and beginners who took a few classes beforehand, people from all backgrounds and abilities. It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. Connect to the community If you want to join the CI Monday Jam WhatsApp group, click on this link: https://chat.whatsapp.com/Iivbz8LzDvK5lGkiitQgcH (when you join please introduce yourself so we know who's in the chat) More events on mariechabert.com https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-s47od-20260713183000

sessions.title: ProDance Class with Kieran Brown
sessions.details: 'A release-based class cultivating awareness through movement. The class aims to develop softness and somatic presence through form, playing with weight and flow to expand and inhabit our dancing bodies through space. We begin on the floor, guided by principles of Feldenkrais to build somatic awareness and awaken the body’s intelligence. Through gentle, intentional exploration of the skeletal structure, attuning to sensation, gradually building heat and structure as we make our way to standing. From this grounded foundation, we transition into improvised crossings, activating the senses through touch. We explore the body’s relationship to gravity—playing with the weight of the limbs, head, and pelvis, and riding the architecture of the body from within. As the class progresses, we learn set material, approaching it with an improvisational sensibility. Inviting this into choreographed phrases that explore soft expansion and length, playing with weight transference and coordination through space.’

sessions.title: ProDance Class with Kieran Brown
sessions.details: 'A release-based class cultivating awareness through movement. The class aims to develop softness and somatic presence through form, playing with weight and flow to expand and inhabit our dancing bodies through space. We begin on the floor, guided by principles of Feldenkrais to build somatic awareness and awaken the body’s intelligence. Through gentle, intentional exploration of the skeletal structure, attuning to sensation, gradually building heat and structure as we make our way to standing. From this grounded foundation, we transition into improvised crossings, activating the senses through touch. We explore the body’s relationship to gravity—playing with the weight of the limbs, head, and pelvis, and riding the architecture of the body from within. As the class progresses, we learn set material, approaching it with an improvisational sensibility. Inviting this into choreographed phrases that explore soft expansion and length, playing with weight transference and coordination through space.’

sessions.title: The Playground
sessions.details: The Playground is an open creative space for Artists across the arts to come together to explore, collaborate and create in a supportive, welcoming environment. For dancers, sessions are aimed at those in their final years of professional training and those already working professionally. Artists from other creative disciplines are warmly welcome to join, create and collaborate. Whether you're looking to move, make, experiment or simply reconnect with your creativity, The Playground is a space to play, connect and be inspired.

sessions.title: Moving Together: Improvisation, Connection & Expression
sessions.details: In this class, James guides participants through improvisation practices that encourage honesty, curiosity, and personal expression through movement. Together, we will explore how to connect more deeply with ourselves, our bodies, and each other in a supportive and open environment. Through guided tasks and shared exploration, the class invites participants to discover joy in both dancing and witnessing others dance, while building a sense of community and connection. CLASS DESCRIPTION: Do you want to limit your injury risk, while also building strength to become a better dancer? This fitness class will help you substantially improve your posture and correct any issues relating to your body alignment. It is very easy to create bad habits in ballet, so changing these habits often requires retraining muscle memory. Christina's Posture Power with PBT elements class will not only help you build up more strength and flexibility, but will also help you train the muscle memory required for automatically performing movements the right way. This class will be accompanied by music. With her experience as a coach, ballet teacher and approved PBT instructor, Christina has put together a class that will help you limit your injury risk and become a stronger and better dancer. Posture Power with PBT elements is a general level class and therefore suitable for those, who either wish to improve their ballet technique or simply improve their fitness level. It is also a perfect preparation for her 11:30 Int/Adv ballet class which takes place right after her Posture Power with PBT elements class. Progressing Ballet Technique (PBT) is an innovative programme which was developed by Marie Walton- Mahon in order to help dancers and students improve their technique. The programme includes carefully designed exercises focusing on training muscle memory and improving core strength, weight placement and alignment of the body. Minimum age: 14

CLASS DESCRIPTION This class will follow the traditional structure of the codified technique, sequencing through a set series of seated floor exercises, standing exercises and across-the-floor sequences. The Graham Technique is an immensely valuable technique to layer on top of any dance training as it emphasises the importance of the usage of the back, as well as accessing the deep core abdominal muscles.Fundamental principles in Graham Technique are the contraction and release, opposition, shift of weight and spirals. Graham dancers believe that it is important that we not simply see ourselves as objects in space when dancing, but that we expand their body, energy and focus so they are amplified enough to fill that space. The class will serve to free up the back, open up the hips and the body. On top, form the dancer to find dynamics, intricacy and articulation of the spine. Minimum age: 16

sessions.title: Monday Contact Improv: Class + Jam
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 5SQ • Doors open at 6.20pm Please note they won't be an intro circle anymore. First timers can arrive a bit earlier for any questions and info around consent or about the jam. I also advise newcomers to familiarise themselves with the guidelines. This week we have a class taught by Marie, an experienced CI practitioner (22 years), professional dancer and choreographer. Theme and Content The theme of the class will be posted closer to the time in the CI Monday Jam WhatsApp group. You can join in following this link: https://chat.whatsapp.com/Iivbz8LzDvK5lGkiitQgcH (please note I will ask you a few question about yourself before I allow you into the chat, when you join please introduce yourself so we know who's in the chat) These Contact Improvisation classes give participants tools to be in touch and communicate through touch, and feel more confident joining a jam. There are open levels and benefit beginners, improvers and experienced practitioners. There is a mix of somatic guided exploration to be embodied, usually in solo, some mindful and focused explorations with one or several partners, and some more technical tools or short patterns. This will be followed by a 45min-1h jam Jam The emphasis of the jam is to explore movement while being in physical contact with other movers. Participants are encouraged to experience it as an embodied research and a practice where everyone can bring their own research, interest and physicality into the space. Jamming is the best way to try out, take risks, learn from each other, observe, connect, be surprised, practice setting boundaries, dance and play with people we may not know or expect to dance with. Participants are asked to take responsibility for themselves. Levels and abilities: The space welcomes professional dancers, amateurs, seasoned contact improvisers and beginners, people from all backgrounds and abilities. It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. Event page: https://millco.co.uk/events/contact-improvisation-jam/ https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-so6jw-20260720183000

sessions.title: Monday Contact Improv: Class + Jam
sessions.details: Rose Lipman Building, 43 De Beauvoir Road, London, N1 5SQ • Doors open at 6.20pm Please note they won't be an intro circle anymore. First timers can arrive a bit earlier for any questions and info around consent or about the jam. I also advise newcomers to familiarise themselves with the guidelines. This week we have a class taught by Marie, an experienced CI practitioner (22 years), professional dancer and choreographer. Theme and Content The theme of the class will be posted closer to the time in the CI Monday Jam WhatsApp group. You can join in following this link: https://chat.whatsapp.com/Iivbz8LzDvK5lGkiitQgcH (please note I will ask you a few question about yourself before I allow you into the chat, when you join please introduce yourself so we know who's in the chat) These Contact Improvisation classes give participants tools to be in touch and communicate through touch, and feel more confident joining a jam. There are open levels and benefit beginners, improvers and experienced practitioners. There is a mix of somatic guided exploration to be embodied, usually in solo, some mindful and focused explorations with one or several partners, and some more technical tools or short patterns. This will be followed by a 45min-1h jam Jam The emphasis of the jam is to explore movement while being in physical contact with other movers. Participants are encouraged to experience it as an embodied research and a practice where everyone can bring their own research, interest and physicality into the space. Jamming is the best way to try out, take risks, learn from each other, observe, connect, be surprised, practice setting boundaries, dance and play with people we may not know or expect to dance with. Participants are asked to take responsibility for themselves. Levels and abilities: The space welcomes professional dancers, amateurs, seasoned contact improvisers and beginners, people from all backgrounds and abilities. It requires every participants to take responsibility for their own bodies, so if you need extra support or a carer or someone to look after you then you can bring them for free. Note for beginners: the jam is not guided. The facilitator is there to hold the space but doesn't guide the jam. What is Contact Improvisation (CI)? Contact Improvisation is movement research that explores the physical principles of touch, momentum, and shared weight in relation to gravity. It involves a constant dialogue between two or more movers who respond to each other’s movements in real time, often maintaining physical contact but also playing with proximity and space. This practice emphasises spontaneity, trust, and mutual awareness, allowing dancers to create unique movement for each encounter. Event page: https://millco.co.uk/events/contact-improvisation-jam/ https://bookwhen.com/mariechabert/e/ev-so6jw-20260720183000

You can wear whatever your are comfortable moving in, and you’re welcome to wear dance shoes if you have them (although no dark/black soles) or bare-feet. Please make sure you have removed jewellery before class, and long hair is tied back. Please note, as the studios are used by our professional dancers we ask that you refrain from using hair products and body lotions as these can make the floor slippery. BIOBorn and raised in California, Tiffany began training at the San Francisco Ballet School at the age of 12. Her first professional engagement was with Boston Ballet II, followed by four seasons with Miami City Ballet. She then returned to Boston Ballet, where she was promoted to the rank of soloist. In 2014, Tiffany joined English National Ballet, also as a soloist, and remained with the company for ten and a half years—bringing her total professional career to an impressive 24 years.CLASS DESCRIPTIONThe class is geared for professionals, pre professionals and advanced students over 14 years of age. It is important to get a sense of what professional company class is like, so I feel it’s important to bring that atmosphere into the studio. It is relatively simple for the mind to retain, so we can focus on honing our skills and warming up our body’s in the proper way. I promote a positive and safe environment that encourages you reach your goals.

CLASS DESCRIPTION: Do you want to limit your injury risk, while also building strength to become a better dancer? This fitness class will help you substantially improve your posture and correct any issues relating to your body alignment. It is very easy to create bad habits in ballet, so changing these habits often requires retraining muscle memory. Christina's Posture Power with PBT elements class will not only help you build up more strength and flexibility, but will also help you train the muscle memory required for automatically performing movements the right way. This class will be accompanied by music. With her experience as a coach, ballet teacher and approved PBT instructor, Christina has put together a class that will help you limit your injury risk and become a stronger and better dancer. Posture Power with PBT elements is a general level class and therefore suitable for those, who either wish to improve their ballet technique or simply improve their fitness level. It is also a perfect preparation for her 11:30 Int/Adv ballet class which takes place right after her Posture Power with PBT elements class. Progressing Ballet Technique (PBT) is an innovative programme which was developed by Marie Walton- Mahon in order to help dancers and students improve their technique. The programme includes carefully designed exercises focusing on training muscle memory and improving core strength, weight placement and alignment of the body. Minimum age: 14

CLASS DESCRIPTION: Do you want to limit your injury risk, while also building strength to become a better dancer? This fitness class will help you substantially improve your posture and correct any issues relating to your body alignment. It is very easy to create bad habits in ballet, so changing these habits often requires retraining muscle memory. Christina's Posture Power with PBT elements class will not only help you build up more strength and flexibility, but will also help you train the muscle memory required for automatically performing movements the right way. CLASS DESCRIPTION This class will follow the traditional structure of the codified technique, sequencing through a set series of seated floor exercises, standing exercises and across-the-floor sequences. sessions.title: Women-only Vocal / Nasheeds (Beginner)
sessions.details: Laban Building • Creekside, London, SE8 3DZ, UK, London • This women-only beginner class is built around movement, rather than by a heavy beat or familiar lyrical structure. Instead of music, the class uses vocals and/or nasheeds, offering a different kind of soundscape for movement that feels stripped back, open and deeply personal. The class is ideal for women who want to step away from secular music or music altogether, and for those who are looking for a space that feels culturally sensitive, private and genuinely welcoming. It is also a beautiful option for women who want to experience dance in a different way, where the body, mind and breath have more space to lead. Movement in this class can feel soft, expressive, grounding, or whatever it needs to be for you. Because there is less sound to lean on, the class creates an eye-opening experience: you are invited to trust your own instincts, your own rhythm and your own interpretation. That can feel honest, freeing and surprisingly liberating. The atmosphere values community, uplift and comfort, so you can come solo or with a friend and feel held in the room. Who it’s for Women looking for a safe, private and culturally sensitive space to dance for the first time or return to movement after a break. Those who value community as much as the dance itself, whether they come solo or with a friend. Women who prefer to move without secular music or without music altogether. Women who want a different sound and a different relationship to movement. What to expect You will begin with a short introduction before moving into a beginner-friendly session that includes guided movement, simple choreography and space for self-expression. The class is designed to help you feel comfortable, supported and free to move at your own pace. Outcome You leave feeling grounded, liberated and more connected to your own movement, with a stronger sense of confidence and self-expression. Practical note Please arrive 10–15 minutes early so you can settle in and get familiar with the space before class begins. Suitable for most fitness levels. If you are pregnant, postnatal or managing an injury, please let the team know in advance so adjustments can be made. What to Wear Anything you feel comfortable in and able to move freely. This class is 18+ only. By purchasing a ticket, you agree to these terms and conditions.

CLASS DESCRIPTION: Do you want to limit your injury risk, while also building strength to become a better dancer? This fitness class will help you substantially improve your posture and correct any issues relating to your body alignment. It is very easy to create bad habits in ballet, so changing these habits often requires retraining muscle memory. Christina's Posture Power with PBT elements class will not only help you build up more strength and flexibility, but will also help you train the muscle memory required for automatically performing movements the right way. This class will be accompanied by music. With her experience as a coach, ballet teacher and approved PBT instructor, Christina has put together a class that will help you limit your injury risk and become a stronger and better dancer. Posture Power with PBT elements is a general level class and therefore suitable for those, who either wish to improve their ballet technique or simply improve their fitness level. It is also a perfect preparation for her 11:30 Int/Adv ballet class which takes place right after her Posture Power with PBT elements class. Progressing Ballet Technique (PBT) is an innovative programme which was developed by Marie Walton- Mahon in order to help dancers and students improve their technique. The programme includes carefully designed exercises focusing on training muscle memory and improving core strength, weight placement and alignment of the body. Minimum age: 14

CLASS DESCRIPTION This class will follow the traditional structure of the codified technique, sequencing through a set series of seated floor exercises, standing exercises and across-the-floor sequences. The Graham Technique is an immensely valuable technique to layer on top of any dance training as it emphasises the importance of the usage of the back, as well as accessing the deep core abdominal muscles.Fundamental principles in Graham Technique are the contraction and release, opposition, shift of weight and spirals. Graham dancers believe that it is important that we not simply see ourselves as objects in space when dancing, but that we expand their body, energy and focus so they are amplified enough to fill that space. The class will serve to free up the back, open up the hips and the body. On top, form the dancer to find dynamics, intricacy and articulation of the spine. Minimum age: 16

sessions.title: YIN  WITH MYOFASCIAL RELEASE
sessions.details: Yin Myofascial Release (Yin MFR) is a slow, nourishing practice that combines long-held Yin poses with massage balls to gently melt away deep tension in the body. We’ll settle into passive stretches for a few minutes at a time, using props to apply steady, mindful pressure to areas like the hips, back, shoulders and feet. This helps release tight fascia, improve mobility, ease soreness and leave you feeling more spacious and hydrated from the inside out. It’s not about pushing, it’s about softening. As the body unwinds, the nervous system shifts into “rest and digest” mode, helping you feel grounded, calm and deeply relaxed. Suitable for most levels, this class is a beautiful way to care for your body, move more freely, and give yourself the reset you didn’t know you needed.

CLASS DESCRIPTION Alice’s floor barre was developed and taught to her by the world renowned ballet teacher, Madame Maria Fay. It is a system based on and complimenting a classical ballet technique. Contrary to other conditioning and workout programmes the floor barre is designed particularly to serve the needs of a dancer. Vital in helping to correct postural faults, shaping and strengthening the physique, enhancing the flexibility of the body as well as aiding and supporting dancer’s’ technique and stamina. It is extremely satisfying for dancers and students, helping raise confidence in their body awareness and ability. This class is not suited for beginners. Minimum age: 13 (Younger with exception, contact reception )

For our terms and conditions click here.If you have any questions or technical issues call 020 7629 6183 or emailmembership@danceworks.com. BIOBorn and raised in California, Tiffany began training at the San Francisco Ballet School at the age of 12. Her first professional engagement was with Boston Ballet II, followed by four seasons with Miami City Ballet. She then returned to Boston Ballet, where she was promoted to the rank of soloist. sessions.title: SELF LYMPHATIC DRAINAGE WORKSHOP
sessions.details: Your lymphatic system is one of the body’s most important yet often overlooked systems. Responsible for helping move waste, excess fluid and cellular debris, it plays a vital role in how we look, feel and function. In this workshop, you’ll learn a simple and effective self-lymphatic drainage routine designed to support the face, head, neck, abdomen and legs. Through gentle touch, breath and movement, you’ll discover how to encourage flow throughout the body and develop a deeper understanding of how your own system works. This is not about quick fixes or complicated protocols. It’s about learning practical skills that can become part of your regular self-care routine. Expect to leave feeling lighter, calmer, clearer and more connected to your body, with a routine you can return to whenever you need it. Many people choose to attend monthly or quarterly, using the workshop as a dedicated reset for both body and mind. Over time, the techniques become second nature, allowing you to confidently support your own lymphatic health at home. Simple. Empowering. Something you’ll use for life. HOW TO PREPARE Please arrive well hydrated and, if possible, drink a little water before the workshop. Wear comfortable clothing that allows you to move and easily access areas such as the collarbones, neck and abdomen. Leggings, joggers, shorts, a vest or a loose-fitting top are all perfect. We’ll be working with self-massage around the collarbones, face, neck and belly, so it’s helpful to avoid anything too tight or restrictive. Loose enough trousers that can be gently pulled down at the waist to access the lower abdomen are ideal. As we’ll be moving from a workout into the lymphatic workshop, comfort is key. Please also bring: * A small, clean face towel. * Clean hands and a clean face ready for the session. * Your own face and body oil (or cream) that you’re happy to apply to your skin, as we’ll be working on both the face and full body. No experience is needed — just bring yourself, an open mind and your own two hands.

sessions.title: Rueda Libre Social at The Barbican
sessions.details: We have been invited to return to the Barbican to host one of our socials as part of their Play Make Do festival. Event Tickets: https://ruedalibre.co.uk/Barbican Please gain entry tickets from here Here is a little bit more information on the festival and what is on offer The Barbican invites visitors of all ages to celebrate the return of Play Make Do, a three-day festival packed with free and affordable activities designed to bring families, friends and communities together through creativity, play and participation. Taking place across the Barbican’s public spaces from Friday 14 – Sunday 16 August 2026, Play Make Do transforms the Centre into a vibrant playground for imagination and discovery with circus play, dance, craft, storytelling and more. Inspired by community, summertime and togetherness, this year’s festival also draws on themes of carnival, identity and culture, connecting with ideas explored in the Project a Black Planet exhibition and the wider season programme, running throughout the summer until 6 September. Play Make Do builds on the success of its inaugural edition in 2025, celebrating the creativity that emerges when generations come together to ‘play’, ‘make’ and ‘do’. Each day of the festival is shaped around one of these themes, encouraging visitors to experience the Barbican in new and inspiring ways. PLAY Friday’s programme, PLAY, is dedicated to imagination, movement and discovery. Families can explore the art of clowning with Clowns without Borders UK and circus-play collective Reallynice, or step inside Peut-Être Theatre‘s playful Audiomoves BoogiePod to explore movement, imagination and self-expression. Visitors can also enjoy storytelling with Maryam Hashemi and Barbican Library in the Conservatory, create cyanotype artworks with artists Safiye Gray and Sneha Alexander, and end the day on a musical journey through Colombia with Montañera. MAKE Saturday’s programme, MAKE, invites audiences to spend the day crafting, creating and collaborating. Inspired by Carnival traditions and self-expression, participants can create masks, accessories and headpieces with Tropical Isles Carnival Art of Mas Workshop, contribute to a collective artwork in Black Girl Knit Club’s Braided Traditions workshop, and enjoy stories, songs and rhythms with Barbican Library and drummer Seneke from Mbilla Arts. Families are invited to picnic at the Barbican, make use of the Kitchen’s Kids Eat Free offer for under 10s, and spend the day enjoying summer creativity together. DO Sunday’s programme, DO, closes the weekend with a day of dance, music, celebration and participation. Audiences can try hip hop street dance styles with our Artistic Associates Boy Blue, take part in Bollywood-inspired movement with Bollyqueer, discover the rhythms and culture of Bullerengue Circle, and round off the festival at a Rueda Libre salsa social. Visitors can also enjoy the Sankofa Community Carnival-inspired performance, featuring artists from Mahogany Carnival Design, IRIE! dance theatre and Endurance Steel Orchestra. The Conservatory offers a quieter space for creativity, including Travels in History, a creative writing workshop with award-winning children’s author Claire Linney, exploring Black British history, and Take It Slow: Making Space, a relaxed drop-in drawing session for all ages. Oluwatoyin Odunsi, Senior Producer, Creative Collaboration, Barbican, said: “We’re delighted to welcome families and communities back to Play Make Do. This festival celebrates the creativity, learning and fun that happens when people of all ages make things together. We’ve brought together outstanding artists and collaborators to lead joyful, hands-on experiences. From circus play and storytelling to Carnival-making and dance, the weekend invites audiences to connect, explore the Barbican in new ways, and leave inspired to keep playing, making and doing long after the summer ends.” Karena Johnson, Head of Creative Collaboration, Barbican, said: “Creating opportunities for people to play, connect and express themselves is at the heart of what we do. Play Make Do continues our commitment to opening up the Barbican as a creative civic space for everyone, where audiences can encounter exceptional artists, celebrate different cultural traditions, and explore their own creativity. We want everyone who joins us to feel welcomed, inspired and that this public space belongs to them.” Activities and events are designed to be enjoyed by all ages, with many free for under 18s, and other events free for the whole family. Play Make Do is an inclusive and welcoming summer destination for families, local communities and visitors from across London.

CLASS DESCRIPTION This class will follow the traditional structure of the codified technique, sequencing through a set series of seated floor exercises, standing exercises and across-the-floor sequences. The Graham Technique is an immensely valuable technique to layer on top of any dance training as it emphasises the importance of the usage of the back, as well as accessing the deep core abdominal muscles.Fundamental principles in Graham Technique are the contraction and release, opposition, shift of weight and spirals. Graham dancers believe that it is important that we not simply see ourselves as objects in space when dancing, but that we expand their body, energy and focus so they are amplified enough to fill that space. The class will serve to free up the back, open up the hips and the body. On top, form the dancer to find dynamics, intricacy and articulation of the spine. Minimum age: 16

sessions.title: QUEER DANCE DAYFEST presented by STRUT and QUEER LINE DANCE CLUB
sessions.details: From sultry salsa to Bollywood balle balle, and country bootscootin' to Scottish skipping, social dancing in the queer community is having a real renaissance. People are increasingly craving spaces where they can learn, connect and bask in the magical energy created by moving their bodies to music in unison.To celebrate this growing movement and the diversity of the queer social dance scene, we're taking over the huge event space at Big Penny Social to bring together 5 different collectives and dance styles for the first time ever. ★ STRUT x QLDC QUEER LINE DANCING ★ BOLLYQUEER ★ QUEER SALSA ★ BOOTS QUEER COUNTRY PARTNER DANCING ★ QUEER CEILIDH Come try your hand (and feet) at something new, meet other dance-curious people in a low-stakes, welcoming environment, and maybe discover your next obsession. Respectful allies welcome. All sessions are completely beginner friendly and all partner dancing is non-gendered.Limited number of party only tickets available but you'll miss out on all the lessons. ★ Doors at 1pm, first session at 2pm ★ 5 x 45min sessions – learn the basics and get a taste of each dance flavour. ★ Dance party 8:30-11pm – show off the moves you've learnt and any you already know. ★ Breaks in between sessions to catch your breath, eat, drink, chat and chill ★ Huge food and beer hall ★ Gorgeous garden space and Big Penny Beach ★ Flukes games room with pool, darts and shuffleboard Come dance with us. POLICYSTRUT, QUEER LINE DANCE CLUB and BIG PENNY SOCIAL are spaces which prioritise the safety, comfort, community and joy of LGBTQIA+ people. There is a zero tolerance policy for any forms of homophobia, transphobia, racism, ableism, bigotry, harassment and violence.
